title: _revision_index.json -- DAO-owned source-text revision history v0.1
description: Part 11J. The append-only record of every registered source-text revision for each document in a case, plus which revision is currently the one every offset, evidence quote, and source-derived UID is expressed against. DAO-OWNED: no agent may write this file, and no generic write-contract or patch-manifest path may insert, change, delete, or roll back its contents -- the DAO derives every field from what it observes at registration time. This exists because processed text used to be rewritten in place, which destroyed the bytes a previously-issued UID was computed from and made 'was that UID ever legitimate?' permanently unanswerable. Keeping superseded revisions keeps that question answerable. uid_stability and extractor provenance live on each REVISION, not on the document: recording them per-document would erase the fact that different revisions were produced by different extractors, which is exactly what a re-extraction changes.

documents.description: One entry per document that has at least one registered source-text revision.

current_revision_sha256.description: The revision every current offset, quote, and source-derived UID is expressed against. Flipped LAST in the revision transaction, after downstream invalidation has already been applied, so this pointer never names a revision whose dependents still claim to be passed.

uid_scheme.description: DAO-owned. 'legacy' means UIDs on this document's contracts were never verified against a canonical derivation -- readable and migratable, but not writable as new work. 'canonical_v1' means every UID is recomputed and must match. Activation is a dedicated, verified DAO command (commit c); downgrade is refused outright, because a switch that can be turned back off is not a guarantee, it is a bypass -- writing an arbitrary UID would only require flipping the scheme down first.

revisions.description: Append-only. A superseded revision is never deleted: it is what makes a previously-issued UID recomputable, and therefore auditable.

revision.description: One registered version of a document's processed source text, with the provenance the DAO observed when it was registered.

revision_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact registered text bytes. Also the revision file's name under data/processed/{case}/{doc}/_revisions/.

registered_by.description: The --held-by of the DAO call that registered it. Accountability, not authority: it grants nothing.

uid_stability.description: DAO-DERIVED from the manifest's extraction_method, never declared by an agent -- a self-declared stability claim is the same shape as the self-certified review D2 exists to prevent. 'deterministic_source' (embedded_text): re-extracting the same immutable PDF reproduces these bytes, so a changed UID means a real change or a bug. 'ocr_derived': extraction is non-deterministic, so a re-extraction may legitimately alter span bytes and therefore alter UIDs of the spans whose reading changed -- that is honest, not a fault. 'unknown': extraction_method was absent or unrecognized; no stability claim is made rather than a convenient one being assumed.

page_text_sha256.description: Per-page digests of the registered text, so a change can be localized to the pages that actually moved instead of only being visible as a whole-document difference.

supersedes.description: The revision this one replaced, or null for the first. Makes the chain explicit rather than inferring it from array order.

extractor_profile.description: The extraction identity the DAO observed, recorded so a profile CHANGE is detectable and treated as a new derivation. Deliberately not treated as proof of sameness: the extractors here are external CLIs whose model deployments change without any version string moving, so 'the profile is unchanged' does not establish 'the derivation is unchanged'. Detecting change is reliable; inferring sameness is not, and that asymmetry is recorded rather than papered over (see known-gaps).

extraction_method.description: Mirrors the manifest's extraction_method at registration time.

tool.description: The DAO entry point that registered the revision.

profile_sha256.description: Digest of the observed profile fields, so a change is a single comparison.
